chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from some of his companions, from some of the Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and confessed to theft. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) asked him: 'Do you recite anything from the Book of Allah?' He said: 'Yes, Surah Al-Baqarah.' He said: 'I have granted you pardon for your hand on account of Surah Al-Baqarah.'

Al-Ash'ath said: 'Do you nullify a punishment (hadd) of Allah the Exalted?' He said: 'And what do you know about this? When the evidence is established, it is not for the Imam to pardon; but when the man confesses to himself, that is up to the Imam: if he wishes, he pardons, and if he wishes, he cuts.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between pardoning a thief through confession versus evidence in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between pardon (afw) and punishment (qatf) in theft cases, emphasizing that the Imam's discretion to waive the hadd applies specifically when the offender confesses, whereas established evidence removes this discretion. The reference to Surah Al-Baqarah highlights the spiritual merit of Quranic knowledge as a mitigating factor, reflecting the Shia view that judicial discretion is tied to the mode of proof. This principle underscores the balance between divine law and the Imam's authority to exercise mercy based on specific legal conditions.
